summary: Zolmitriptan is a selective serotonin 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist (triptan) indicated for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults (and, for the nasal spray, in patients 12 years and older). It is not for prophylaxis and is not established for cluster headache. It is available as oral tablets, orally disintegrating tablets, and a nasal spray. The recommended oral starting dose is 2.5 mg, which may be repeated after at least 2 hours, up to a maximum of 10 mg in 24 hours; the nasal spray starting dose is 2.5 mg with a maximum single dose of 5 mg and a 24-hour maximum of 10 mg. Its action is attributed to agonism at 5-HT1B/1D receptors causing cranial vasoconstriction and inhibition of pro-inflammatory neuropeptide release from trigeminal nerves. It is contraindicated in ischemic coronary, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular disease, certain accessory-pathway arrhythmias, uncontrolled hypertension, hemiplegic/basilar migraine, within 24 hours of ergots or another triptan, and within 2 weeks of an MAO-A inhibitor. Serotonin syndrome can occur with serotonergic drugs.
indications: Acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults (oral tablet and orally disintegrating tablet)
Acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older (nasal spray)

dosage.d: 2.5 mg single dose; may repeat after at least 2 hours if needed; maximum 10 mg in 24 hours
dosage.t: A 5 mg single dose may be used; 2.5 mg or lower is advised in hepatic impairment
dosage.n: If first dose fails, reconsider the diagnosis

dosage.d: 2.5 mg (one spray) starting dose; maximum single dose 5 mg; may repeat after 2 hours; maximum 10 mg in 24 hours
Moderate to severe impairment: use a low dose (e.g. <=2.5 mg oral) with caution; nasal spray not recommended in moderate-severe impairment

admin: Take as early as possible after the migraine begins; can be taken at any point during an attack
Separate repeat doses by at least 2 hours; do not exceed 10 mg in 24 hours
Orally disintegrating tablets are placed on the tongue and dissolve - do not use with liquid and do not split
Prime the nasal spray per the instructions; one spray delivers the dose into a single nostril
Assess cardiovascular risk before the first dose; consider a supervised first dose / ECG in at-risk patients
Do not use within 24 hours of an ergotamine-type medicine or another triptan, or within 2 weeks of an MAO-A inhibitor
moa: Zolmitriptan binds with high affinity to 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptors. Its therapeutic activity in migraine is attributed to agonism at these receptors on intracranial blood vessels (including arteriovenous anastomoses) and on sensory nerves of the trigeminal system. Receptor stimulation produces vasoconstriction of dilated cranial vessels and inhibits the release of pro-inflammatory and vasoactive neuropeptides, reducing neurogenic inflammation and transmission of nociceptive signals. An active N-desmethyl metabolite has similar 5-HT1B/1D agonist activity and contributes to the effect.

absolute: Ischemic coronary artery disease (angina, prior MI, documented silent ischemia) or coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal's angina)
Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome or arrhythmias with other cardiac accessory conduction pathway disorders
History of stroke or transient ischemic attack
Peripheral vascular disease, including ischemic bowel disease
Use within 24 hours of another 5-HT1 agonist (triptan) or an ergotamine-type medication
Concurrent use or use within 2 weeks of an MAO-A inhibitor
relative: Cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, diabetes, smoking, obesity, strong family history, postmenopausal women, men >40) - assess before use
Concurrent serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs) - serotonin syndrome risk
Moderate to severe hepatic impairment (reduce dose)
monitor: Cardiovascular symptoms (chest/throat/jaw tightness or pain) after dosing

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of zolmitriptan in pregnant women. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Animal studies showed embryolethality and fetal abnormalities at high doses.
lact: It is not known whether zolmitriptan is excreted in human milk at clinically relevant amounts (it is excreted in animal milk). Exercise caution when administering to a breastfeeding woman and consider minimising infant exposure.
renal: Zolmitriptan and its metabolites are partly renally eliminated. Clearance is reduced in patients with severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <=15 mL/min); use with caution in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Zolmitriptan is extensively metabolised by the liver, so plasma concentrations rise in hepatic impairment. In patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment, use a low oral dose (e.g. <=2.5 mg) with caution and consider blood-pressure monitoring; the nasal spray is not recommended in moderate to severe hepatic impairment.

major: MAO-A inhibitors (markedly increase zolmitriptan exposure - contraindicated, including within 2 weeks of stopping)
Ergotamine / dihydroergotamine and other ergot-type medicines (additive prolonged vasospasm - do not use within 24 hours)
Other 5-HT1 agonists / triptans (additive vasospastic effects - separate by 24 hours)
moderate: Cimetidine (inhibits zolmitriptan metabolism - consider lower max dose, e.g. 5 mg/24h)
Other CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g. fluvoxamine, some quinolones) may raise levels
Oral contraceptives may increase zolmitriptan plasma concentrations
minor: Tricyclic antidepressants, lithium, tramadol, St John's Wort (additive serotonergic effect)
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interaction; may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No direct pharmacologic interaction, but alcohol can precipitate migraine
interactions.diagnostics: Transient blood-pressure elevation may occur; no specific lab interference

common: Sensation of warmth, heaviness, pressure or tightness (including chest, neck, throat, jaw)
serious: Coronary artery vasospasm / myocardial ischemia or infarction
Peripheral and gastrointestinal vasospasm (ischemic colitis, Raynaud-like)

monitoring: Cardiovascular risk assessment before the first dose; consider ECG/supervised first dose in at-risk patients
Post-dose symptoms: chest/jaw/throat tightness, palpitations (possible cardiac ischemia)
Signs of serotonin syndrome when combined with serotonergic drugs
Frequency of headache and triptan use (medication-overuse headache)
counsel: Use this only to treat a migraine attack - it does not prevent migraines
Take it as soon as the headache starts; you may repeat once after 2 hours but do not exceed 10 mg in 24 hours
Stop and seek urgent care for chest, jaw, throat, or arm tightness/pain, or palpitations
Do not use within 24 hours of an ergot medicine or another triptan
Tell your doctor about antidepressants (SSRIs/SNRIs) - combined use can cause serotonin syndrome
Using it on too many days per month can cause rebound (medication-overuse) headaches
For the orally disintegrating tablet, let it dissolve on the tongue; for the nasal spray, expect a brief unusual taste
pk: Headache relief typically begins within ~45 minutes to 1 hour (nasal spray faster onset)
Oral Tmax ~2 hours (ODT similar); nasal spray Tmax ~3 hours but early absorption within minutes
Relief over ~2-4 hours; headache may recur, allowing a repeat dose after 2 hours
Store at controlled room temperature (about 20-25 degrees C); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Acute therapy only - not for prophylaxis; if the first dose fails, reconsider the migraine diagnosis.
Contraindicated in ischemic coronary, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular disease, WPW/accessory-pathway arrhythmias, uncontrolled hypertension, and hemiplegic/basilar migraine.
Do not combine with ergots or another triptan within 24 hours; contraindicated with MAO-A inhibitors (and within 2 weeks of stopping).
Cimetidine inhibits metabolism - limit the maximum 24-hour dose (about 5 mg) when co-administered.
Reduce the dose in moderate-severe hepatic impairment; the nasal spray is not recommended in such patients.
Frequent use (more than ~4 headaches/month treated) can cause medication-overuse headache.
missed: Zolmitriptan is taken as needed for an acute migraine, not on a fixed schedule, so there is no 'missed dose'. Do not take extra doses to make up, and do not exceed 10 mg in 24 hours or treat more than the recommended number of attacks. If migraines are frequent, ask your doctor about preventive treatment.
overdose: There is little experience of acute overdose. Subjects given single oral doses of 50 mg commonly experienced sedation. Because the elimination half-life is about 3 hours, monitor patients for at least 15 hours or while symptoms or signs persist. There is no specific antidote. In severe intoxication, provide intensive care including airway protection, oxygenation/ventilation, and cardiovascular monitoring and support. The effect of haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis on plasma concentrations is unknown.
